doc.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Teaching Ellington courses and the Nixon kisses story
summary: Wolff describes his jazz-on-film courses and an Ellington Freedom Award anecdote with Nixon.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: As well as a composer. How often do you get out and do the film presentations?

Well I started teaching these back home for various groups, whether it’s a college, there is an African American college back home that wanted me to a history of jazz, African Americans on film in jazz. So I did a course on that. I teach for various churches and temples back home and I do a four hour class, four sessions, two hours each, of this new course which starts the last two Thursdays of this month and the first two Thursdays of next month. It’s like from 7-9 and it’s all on Ellington. So I have been researching Ellington and putting Ellington together, and I must have at least twelve classes full of material that I can’t choose what I’m going to do. And I put it all together for this class, and now I’ve put so much together I don’t know what I’m going to choose to share.

Well I just don’t know which are my favorites. There is so much. I’ve learned so much. You know you pick up little tidbits. Like I have a film where Nixon gives Ellington the Freedom Award. The highest award for a civilian, in a year or two, when Duke had been snubbed by the Pulitzer Prize Committee. So I have on film where Nixon invites him to the White House and gives him this award, and Duke kisses him two times on the right side and two times on the left side, and in the research I’m doing I learned that after the ceremony was over Duke said — Nixon said to Duke, “I’m not sure I understand the significance of the two kisses on each side; I know you go to Europe a lot and the tradition there is one kiss on each side. So what did this mean?” And The Duke, who has used this on numerous other occasions with women, said to the president, “Why Mr. President, that’s one for each cheek.” So it’s now a story that I’m re-telling.
